title: 1911 M116 Sporting Life Honus Wagner (Blue Background) - PSA VG 3
description: This 1911 M116 Sporting Life Honus Wagner "Blue Background" card grades PSA VG 3. The front pictures Wagner in a head-and-shoulders portrait with a blue sky background fading to green at the shoulders, captioned "Hans Wagner, Pitts. Nationals" beneath the image. The card shows even wear consistent with the VG grade, including softened corners and light surface toning, while the printed colors remain bright and the portrait retains good detail and registration throughout. The reverse carries the Sporting Life advertising back, promoting the publication as the "recognized authority on all base ball matters" for twenty-seven years, available at five cents per copy from newsdealers. A clean, well-centered example of this scarce blue-background variation of the Hall of Fame shortstop's M116 issue, professionally graded and encapsulated by PSA.

title: 2010 National Treasures Signature Patches NBA Logo #1 Stephen Curry (LE 11/12) – BGS GEM MT 9.5, Beckett 10 Auto. (Highest Dual-Graded)
description: This 2010-11 National Treasures Signature Patches NBA Logo card of Stephen Curry is a near-perfect specimen that represents the pinnacle of the modern card collecting hobby. The card features an oversized NBA logoman patch alongside a bold, authenticated on-card autograph from Curry, numbered 11/12, making it one of only twelve examples ever produced. Beckett has graded this card BGS 9.5 Gem Mint with a perfect Beckett 10 autograph — the highest possible authentication of signature quality. The card itself presents Curry in his Golden State Warriors uniform during his second NBA season, when he was beginning to hint at the revolutionary shooting ability that would make him a four-time NBA champion and the greatest three-point shooter in basketball history. Centering grades at 9.5, corners at 9, edges at 9.5, and surface at 9.5 combine for the 9.5 overall. At this time, this is the highest graded example in Beckett's population report, with only four others meeting the 9.5 card grade criteria. With a perfect 10 auto grade, this is the best possible dual grade you can find in the hobby for this elite Steph card.

title: 2006 Upper Deck SP Signature #SPSMJ Michael Jordan Signatures – PSA GEM MINT 10
description: This 2006 SP Signature Edition #SPSMJ has been graded a perfect PSA GEM MINT 10 for the card. It features a striking portrait image of Jordan in his iconic Chicago Bulls #23 jersey, with a bold blue Jordan signature elegantly applied to the card's designated autograph area beneath an ornate decorative border. The PSA 10 designation confirms both the card's physical perfection with four perfectly sharp corners, no print defects, and flawless centering. The signature, which comes via a pre-signed sticker label, is gauranteed autograph by the Upper Deck Company which has represented Michael Jordan exclusively for his trading cards and autographed memoraiblia since 1992. Jordan is universally recognized as the greatest basketball player of all time, having led the Chicago Bulls to six NBA championships, earning six Finals MVP awards and five regular-season MVPs.

title: 1934 Goudey #37 Lou Gehrig – PSA MINT 9 (OC)
description: A premier example of one of the hobby's most desirable Lou Gehrig issues, this 1934 Goudey card presents the Iron Horse smiling broadly in his New York Yankees cap, with a blue "Lou Gehrig says..." caption banner running along the bottom of the card beneath a small inset portrait. The card's vibrant yellow background and sharp lithography remain exceptionally well preserved, with strong corners and clean surfaces throughout. The reverse carries Gehrig's quoted career highlights and personal statistics, including his .343 ten-year batting average and 1933 American League runs-scored title, printed in the set's characteristic green ink over a cream background. PSA has graded this example MINT 9, noting only a slight off-center cut (OC) qualifier, an outstanding grade for this 90-year-old issue. Population reports show just two examples graded this high, making this a true condition-census piece for advanced Gehrig and Goudey collectors.

title: 1951 Bowman #253 Mickey Mantle Rookie (Newly Graded) – PSA VG 3
description: This 1951 Bowman #253 Mickey Mantle true rookie card has just recently been graded VG 3 by PSA. The front pictures Mantle in his right-handed batting pose, looking over his left shoulder in his Yankees cap, with the black "Mickey Mantle" nameplate box at upper right within the lovely sky-and-cloud background artwork. The card's condition suits its grade, with significant vertical off-centering and rounded top corners. The white borders are slightly off-white and the edges appear straight and smooth. The image itself remains bright with fine registration on Mick's face, uniform and bat. Two vertical print lines are barely visible running down his jersey. There are no creases, stains or wrinkles to the surface. The reverse carries Mantle's rookie-year biography, height, weight, and 1950 Joplin minor league stats beneath the "No. 253 in the 1951 Series" heading and Bowman Gum copyright. A certified example of the hobby's most significant post-war "true" rookie card, freshly encapsulated and graded.

title: 1986 Fleer #57 Michael Jordan - PSA GEM MINT 10
description: This 1986 Fleer #57 Michael Jordan rookie card grades PSA GEM MINT 10, the highest grade on the PSA scale. The front pictures Jordan elevating for a one-handed dunk in his red Bulls road uniform, set against the red, white, and blue Fleer border with the "Fleer Premier" banner in the upper corner and "Michael Jordan, Bulls — Guard-Forward" lettered across the bottom. The card presents with four sharp corners, perfect centering within the printed border, and a flawless surface free of any printing imperfections, chipping, or staining — the combination that earned the perfect grade. The reverse carries Jordan's rookie-season statistics, college and personal information, and the "57 of 132" set numbering against the Bulls' red team color block. A pristine example of the hobby's most recognized basketball rookie card, graded at the absolute top of the population.

title: 1949 Casey Stengel New York Yankees World Series Champions 10K Gold Ring – Business Manager LOA
description: Presented is an extraordinary original World Series championship ring awarded to Hall of Fame manager Casey Stengel in recognition of the New York Yankees' 1949 World Championship season. More than simply a championship keepsake, this ring represents the beginning of one of the most remarkable dynasties in sports history. The 1949 title marked the first of an unprecedented five consecutive World Series championships captured under Stengel's leadership—a feat unmatched in Major League Baseball and among the most enduring records in all of professional sports. Crafted by Balfour in 10-karat gold, the ring's elegant design is centered by an approximately 0.35 to 0.55-carat diamond set within a baseball field motif and framed by an ornate floral border. Encircling the centerpiece is the proud designation, "New York Yankees World Champions." Each shank features a matching design highlighted by the year "1949" positioned above the iconic Yankees top hat emblem. The interior band is engraved "Charles Stengel," the Hall of Famer's given name, and bears the manufacturer's "Balfour 10K" hallmark. The ring is a size 9, weighs approximately 27 grams, and displays only minimal wear consis

title: 1968 Bob Gibson Autographed St. Louis Cardinals Game Worn Road Jersey from MVP, Cy Young & Record 1.12 ERA Season – SGC Superior/Excellent
description: The 1968 Major League Baseball season is remembered as "The Year of the Pitcher", when St. Louis Cardinals ace Bob Gibson delivered arguably the most dominant pitching campaign in history. At 32 years old and well into his prime, the 6’ 1” righty from Omaha threw 300-plus innings and finished with a microscopic 1.12 ERA – still the lowest single-season ERA in the live-ball era (post-1920). Gibby went 22-9 with 13 shutouts and 28 complete games in 34 starts, also leading the league in strikeouts with 268. With these numbers, it was no surprise that he easily won both the National League Cy Young and MVP awards. The Cards went on to win the NL pennant thanks to their unhittable horse and nearly completed a dream season, falling just short in a thrilling 7-game World Series against the Detroit Tigers. In Game 1 of that epic Fall Classic, Gibson pitched his final masterpiece of the season, striking out 17 batters – still a World Series record – in a 4-0 complete game shutout. title: 1998 Michael Jordan Chicago Bulls "Last Dance" NBA Finals Game 2 (First Half) Worn Air Jordan XIII Shoes – Sports Investors, Bulls & Jeff Schultz LOAs
description: ADDENDUM: MJ's 2nd half shoes from Game 2 of the 1998 NBA Finals sold for $2.2 million in April 2023. He wore this offered pair in the 1st half and changed at halftime. This is well-documented. Michael Jordan's "The Last Dance" season concluded in true MJ fashion, finding himself in the 1998 NBA Finals facing a hungry Utah Jazz team led by John Stockton and Karl Malone. The Bulls found themselves trailing the series after Game 1 against a loud and energetic Utah crowd. On June 5th, 1998, Michael knew a masterpiece performance was needed in order to head back to Chicago with a 1-1 tie rather than the dreaded 0-2 deficit, especially in the Finals. This wouldn't be the first time Jordan rose to the occasion, and he delivered, recording a game-high 37 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists, as well as a block and a steal. The Bulls won game two in a physical battle, 93-88. Presented in this lot are the game-worn 'Air Jordan XIII' shoes that Jordan wore during the first half of Game 2 of the 1998 NBA Finals and likely beforehand in Game 3 of the 1998 Eastern Conference Finals according to the detailed provenance. title: Incredible C. 1930's Babe Ruth Signed & Inscribed Original Photograph by George Burke – PSA/DNA Type 1
description: This striking original photograph of Babe Ruth, captured by legendary New York sports photographer George Burke, has been neatly signed and inscribed by the Bambino himself, among the most coveted forms of Ruth memorabilia in the hobby. Burke's images of Ruth rank among the most iconic and widely reproduced photographs in baseball history, and this example, a genuine period print rather than a modern reproduction, carries the added significance of Ruth's own hand across its surface. PSA/DNA has examined and certified the autograph on the Type 1 photograph, meaning the signature was applied directly to an original, period-produced print rather than a later reprint, a distinction that dramatically enhances both rarity and value. Ruth-signed photographs of this caliber, bearing bold, full inscriptions, grow harder to source every year as the population of surviving period examples continues to shrink. Given Ruth's stature as the most transcendent figure the game has ever produced, demand for authentic vintage-signed material bearing his autograph remains at the top of the hobby, and Type 1 photographs represent the gold standard for collectors seeking a genuine, contemporaneous artifa

title: 1922 Harry Houdini “The Spirit of Lincoln” Original Photo (1-of-1)  Rarest of The Rare  Image Used in Lincoln Pres. Library & Museum - PSA/DNA Type  1
description: This extraordinary period double-exposure photograph depicts Harry Houdini seated in his signature rope-tied escape pose while the translucent figure of Abraham Lincoln appears behind him. Rather than a supernatural image, the photograph is an authentic period photographic illusion, created by exposing two glass plate negatives to produce a single composite print. Houdini himself titled the image "The Great Liberator Meets the Great Emancipator," pairing his own reputation as the world's greatest escape artist with Lincoln's enduring legacy. Far from promoting belief in the paranormal, Houdini created photographs such as this to expose the deceptive techniques employed by spirit photographers and fraudulent mediums. Throughout the 1920s he staged convincing "spirit" photographs for lectures, press demonstrations, investigations, and publicity, showing audiences just how easily photographic manipulation could manufacture supposed evidence of ghosts—essentially exposing the era's equivalent of what we would today call "Photoshopping." title: 1929 Philadelphia Athletics World Series Champions 18K Solid Gold Ring Presented to 2B Max Bishop
description: This exquisite 1929 Philadelphia Athletics World Series Champions ring, presented to second baseman Max Bishop, is crafted in 18-karat yellow gold with an elegantly detailed band. The face is centered by an old European-cut diamond set within a horseshoe motif, flanked by raised elephant figures — the Athletics' mascot — with "CHAMPIONS" engraved in banner script along one shoulder and "29" worked into the design at the base. The ring shows wear consistent with decades of ownership, including oxidized recesses throughout the engraved detail, scattered surface scratches, and softened high points on the elephant figures, though all design elements and lettering remain fully legible. The interior is stamped "18KT" with a jeweler's mark and is additionally to engraved "MAX BISHOP" identifying the player recipient. A remarkable, well-documented championship ring from baseball's first 3-peat dynasty, presented directly to a member of the 1929 World Series-winning roster. The size 7.5 ring weighs 16 grams.

title: July 4, 1939 Lou Gehrig Delivers “The Luckiest Man Speech” Original Photo by Murray Becker Capturing His Career Defining Masterpiece! – PSA/DNA Type 1
description: Capturing Gehrig alone in an intensely personal moment, this is arguably the most emotional image from one of the most famous speeches in American history! It stands apart as the defining portrait and what some may view as simply the finest image produced that day. While countless photographs survive from Lou Gehrig Appreciation Day showing Gehrig surrounded by teammates, dignitaries, and photographers, intimate portrait images from the ceremony are remarkably scarce. This original Associated Press photograph is one of only a handful of known solo portraits taken during the historic July 4, 1939. On July 4, 1939, just weeks after his ALS diagnosis had ended his legendary streak of 2,130 consecutive games, Gehrig addressed a packed Yankee Stadium on Lou Gehrig Appreciation Day and delivered what would become one of the most celebrated speeches in American history, declaring himself "the luckiest man on the face of the earth." Renowned Associated Press photographer Murray Becker was there to document the occasion, freezing the unforgettable instant in which Gehrig lowers his head and wipes away tears as his composure briefly gives way. title: C. 1937 Babe Ruth Single Signed OAL (Harridge) Baseball wth Direct Provenance – PSA/DNA LOA
description: This circa 1937 single-signed baseball carries a bold Babe Ruth autograph in blue fountain-pen ink across one of the ball's clean panels, accompanied by a PSA/DNA Letter of Authentication and direct provenance noted in the lot description. The signature is large and fully formed, with strong, legible loops in "Babe" and a flowing "Ruth," showing the ink saturation and slight bleeding into the leather typical of period fountain-pen autographs. The ball itself is an Official American League (Harridge) model, with the leather showing even, attractive toning consistent with its age and red stitching that remains bright and intact. There is light soiling scattered across the panels away from the signature, typical of a ball this age that has been carefully preserved. A clean, boldly signed Ruth single-signed baseball with full third-party authentication and documented direct provenance.

title: 1960 Rome Olympics Gold Winner's Medal for Pole Vault Awarded to USA's Don Bragg with Original Case & Participant's Badge – Estate LOA
description: In our 2026 Spring Premier Auction, for the first time in company history, we sold a gold winner’s medal from the 1960 Rome Summer Olympics for $28,800. Now, we have another one to offer – funny how that happens – and it comes in much better condition with the ornate chain and presentation box perfectly intact. What's more? This was the first-place gold medal awarded to American pole vaulter, Don “Tarzan” Bragg, who dominated the event from 1954 to 1960. As a bonus, Bragg’s athlete participant’s badge from the 1960 Rome Games is also included. These historically significant items come directly from his estate. After setting the world indoor record with a vault of 15’ 9½” (4.81 meters) in February 1959, the former 1955 NCAA champion from Villanova won gold at the 1959 Pan American Games that September. Then, at the 1960 USA Olympic Trials, Bragg vaulted 15’ 9¼” (4.80 meters) to set the world outdoor record. title: 1996 NBA 50 Greatest Players Multi-Signed Lithograph (Legends Edition #6/50) – David Stern & Sam Battistone COA, PSA/DNA LOA
description: This 1996 NBA 50 Greatest Players multi-signed lithograph is numbered 6/50 from the Legends Edition, featuring individual portrait photos of all 50 honorees arranged in rows beneath the "National Basketball Association 50 Greatest Players, 1946-1996" title. Each living honoree has signed directly beneath his own photograph in bold pencil, with the late Pete Maravich's panel left appropriately unsigned and captioned "1947-1988" in his place. The unframed lithograph remains in outstanding condition, with all 50 signatures – 49 living players plus NBA Commissioner David Stern – appearing strong and legible on the 25" by 39" canvas sheet. This comprehensive, fully assembled multi-signed display piece brings together the signatures of the league's most celebrated honorees in a single limited-edition format. Includes full LOA from PSA/DNA (to be uploaded shortly) and certificate of authenticity signed by David Stern and Sam Battistone. It was Battistone, founder of the memorabilia company Field of Dreams and former owner of the Utah Jazz, and Commissioner Stern who formulated the "NBA's 50 Greatest Players" lithograph in 1996.

title: 1981 Ozzie Smith Autographed San Diego Padres Game Worn Road Jersey Photomatched to 1982 Topps Card – Sports Investors LOA, GRAD Auth.
description: Worn and signed by Ozzie Smith during his time with the San Diego Padres, this road jersey has been photo-matched to Smith's 1982 Topps card, providing verified visual confirmation that this exact jersey was worn during a documented, specific moment captured on cardboard (card image shown for reference only). Eventually a first-ballot Hall of Famer and widely regarded as the greatest defensive shortstop in baseball history, Smith began his career with the Padres before being traded to the St. Louis Cardinals where he became known as "The Wizard" and a 13-time Gold Glover. Padres-era Ozzie Smith memorabilia is considerably scarcer than material from his Cardinals tenure, both because his time in San Diego was comparatively brief and because his Cardinals years produced the bulk of his career highlights and postseason moments. For Padres collectors, Ozzie Smith specialists, and those seeking early-career material from a Hall of Fame shortstop before his signature stardom in St. Louis, this photo-matched jersey represents a rare and exceptionally well-documented offering. Includes photo-match LOA from Sports Investors Authentication. The autograph has been certified by Steve Grad.

title: Amazing 1982 Michael Jackson Signed Original Vinyl "Thriller"Album with Period Autograph – Audio Media Grading, PSA/DNA, Beckett & JSA LOAs
description: Presented is an exceptional original gatefold pressing of Thriller, personally signed by Michael Jackson across the iconic front cover in bold black marker. Accompanied by its original vinyl record and lyric insert, this complete first-era example represents one of the most coveted signed music collectibles from the modern recording era. The signature dates to the early 1980s, contemporaneous with the album's meteoric rise following its 1982 release. Universally recognized as the best-selling album of all time, Thriller transformed popular music and established Michael Jackson as the undisputed "King of Pop." Authentic signed examples from this landmark period are increasingly scarce, particularly complete gatefold copies with strong presentation and premium authentication. The album has been professionally encapsulated by Audio Media Grading (AMG) and designated Authentic – Open, preserving both the signature and the complete record package. The autograph is further supported by full Letters of Authenticity from PSA/DNA, Beckett Authentication Services (BAS), and James Spence Authentication (JSA), providing the highest level of confidence for collectors. title: 5/21/1989 Isiah Thomas Detroit Pistons (NBA Champions) Game Worn Shoes Photomatched to Eastern Conference Finals Game 1 – RAI PhotoMatching LOA
description: Offered here is a pair of game-worn Converse Cons ERX 300 sneakers worn by Isiah Thomas during the 1989 Eastern Conference Finals, Game 1, played May 21, 1989, a series the Pistons would win en route to their first NBA Championship, a title they clinched with a sweep of the Los Angeles Lakers in the Finals. The shoes are rendered in Detroit's signature white, blue, and red colorway, with the "PISTONS" script along the heel, star-and-chevron Converse branding on the lateral and medial panels, and the classic "CONS" wordmark on the gum outsole. Both shoes show honest, game-used wear consistent with high-level competition: creasing across the toe box, scuffing along the outsole and midsole, and soiling throughout from floor contact, all indicative of extended on-court use during a physically demanding playoff series. Photomatching was conducted by RAI PhotoMatching, a recognized authority in the authentication space, which compared this pair against photographic imagery from the May 21, 1989 contest, matching wear patterns, scuffing, and other unique characteristics unique to this pair. The shoes come accompanied by a corresponding RAI PhotoMatching Letter of Authenticity. Isiah Thoma
